newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX to extend pit trading hours for Euroyen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX to extend pit trading hours for Euroyen.

text.p: Singapore's futures exchange said on Thursday it plans to extend the pit trading session for Euroyen futures and options from next month, but dealers said the move was unlikely to stir added interest in the contracts.

The Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX) said in a circular to its members that trading time for the Japanese interest rate futures and options contracts would be extended by an hour to 1205 GMT with effect from October 15.

The move was to avoid widening the gap between the close of pit trading on SIMEX and the opening of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) floor as Chicago returns from daylight savings to normal trading hours, the exchange said.
SIMEX and CME established a mutual offset system for the trading of Euroyen futures on March 6, shortly before a similar arrangement was launched between Tokyo and London's futures exchanges.
Under the SIMEX/CME link-up, first established for Eurodollar, or U.S. interest rate futures in 1984, traders can take positions on one exchange and offset them on the other.
"We'll now have to sit in the office for 13 hours a day and I doubt even Singaporean clients will trade (the Euroyen) during that extra hour," said a dealer with a European institution.

Dealers said the extended hours were unlikely to be lifted once Chicago returned to daylight savings time next year and that they, viewed the move more as an attempt by SIMEX to raise its stake in the competition between exchanges.
"The Euroyen is already almost covered round the clock. Why do they want to eat into the London hours," said a dealer with another European house.
He said the contract could already be traded on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) during the interval between SIMEX and CME.

The Euroyen contract tended to be thinly traded outside Asian hours, due to the absence of market-moving news and the fact that the Tokyo International Financial Futures Exchange, which sees the highest Euroyen volume, is closed then, he said.

But a dealer with a U.S. institution said the extended hours could lead to added turnover in Euroyen futures as the only after-hours option currently available to traders was the screen-based Automated Trading System (ATS).
"I think it's good in the sense that the ATS system has not really taken off because the bids and offers are kind of far apart and they hardly move all night," he said.
The SIMEX circular, made available to Reuters, said trading of Euroyen futures on the automated system would also start one hour later at 1235 GMT from October 15.
